pipeline: Phase 3 logreg head → predicted intent + confidence for the message
Phase 4 FAISS index → top-K most similar historical evidence pairs
Grounded prompt: customer message + intent/confidence + evidence quality + the K historical pairs, under six non-negotiable safety rules
LLM draft (z-ai-web-dev-sdk, backend-only) → one Twitter-length reply
Transparent heuristic scoring: grounding overlap, unsupported specifics, safety framing, escalation consistency
safety_rules: 1. Use only facts, troubleshooting steps and phrasing present in the evidence cases. Never invent prices, dates, software versions, policies, phone numbers or links.

2. Include a brief grounding phrase making clear the suggestion comes from how similar issues were handled historically — e.g. "Based on similar cases we've seen, …" — and never imply it is current company policy.
3. If the evidence does not clearly address the customer's issue, do not guess: say you'd like to look into it with them and ask ONE short clarifying question.
4. For account, payment or security matters, never ask for or repeat personal details in public — invite the customer to continue in Direct Messages, exactly as the historical support team did.
5. Style: warm, concise, professional; match the evidence replies. No hashtags, no emoji, no signatures, no quotation marks around the reply.
6. Length: at most 280 characters, one short paragraph (or two sentences).

prompt_design.user_prompt_template: customer message · predicted intent (Phase 3 head confidence, runner-up) · evidence quality (top-1 cosine vs threshold) · the top-5 historical pairs (customer + support text, intent) · instruction to follow every safety rule

grounding_overlap.definition: share of the reply's content tokens (len>=3, stopword-filtered) that appear in the top-K evidence pairs' text

unsupported_specifics.definition: numbers / version-like tokens / prices / URLs in the reply that appear nowhere in the evidence

escalation_consistency.definition: among replies whose Phase 6 gates fail (intent confidence < threshold OR top similarity < threshold): the reply asks a clarifying question or redirects to DMs instead of asserting specific advice

honest_caveats: Token-overlap grounding is a lexical proxy: a reply can be faithful while using fresh wording, or unfaithful while reusing evidence words. No semantic entailment verification was performed.
LLM outputs are nondeterministic; the metrics below describe the recorded run (see generated_at), not a stable property of the pipeline.
No human annotation or preference test was performed — no claim is made that the replies are subjectively 'good', only that the measured grounding and safety proxies hold.
The unsupported-specifics check covers numbers, version-like tokens, prices and URLs; fabricated prose claims would not be caught by it.
Escalation consistency is a preview of the Phase 6 policy; the policy itself is not implemented yet.
